title: Clarifying the Rochester push and film accidents
summary: Nierenberg questions the fight, and Bubbles insists Rochester meant no harm and compares the other film accident, an electrician pulling a switch too fast.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Right, when he pushed you then you pushed him back.
I didn't have to push him back, I couldn't push him back. I'm out. I hit against the table and knocked myself out -- against the top of my spine.
But you said that he came towards you gave him a push --

Look, when he pushed me against the table he's going to jump on me and when he's going to jump on me, I put my feet up and he jumps on my feet and I shove him with my feet -- messed up his suit, that wasn't as much as I was messed up.
No. No. He just played his part that's all. But I figure he was overplaying his part myself.
Yeah. He didn't mean to hurt me. I'm sure he didn't. Nobody wanted to hurt anybody, I don't think.
How do you account for the two films that you made, you got hurt in both?

Well, accidents do happen. This was my stunt I'd do here but it was understood he was going to push me, I was going to take a little lighter lift when I got to the table, they were going to make me hit that table with my hip here, instead of back up here at the top of my spine. See, that's the difference and that's what knocked me out And the other one, the electrician pulled the switch too fast. So accidents do happen, you know. But I made them, thank goodness.
